behavior: Native Free reads the block header, calls the user callback, and only then rewires a recyclable header or releases backing. Its callback type is not noexcept; a thrown callback leaves the storage live. Rust previously removed the safe live-handle entry before notification, making storage inaccessible after callback panic.

Free now validates and reads rounded size, invokes the existing callback, and retires the safe live handle only after the callback returns. Existing small/medium free-list and large-release routes are unchanged. Both original regression cases were red before this correction.

Small pool, medium heap and large heap Free callback failures preserve payload and live handle, do not create a purgeable free entry, and can be retried. Exact event shapes include both failed and successful Free notifications. Completed retry makes the safe handle invalid.

Allocate callback failure preserves the captured allocation for explicit cleanup. Reallocate failure in Allocate leaves old payload unchanged and new storage uncopied. Failure in old-block Free occurs after copying the entire old rounded payload and preserves both allocations. Captured handles are explicitly repaired after catch_unwind.

Fitting Reallocate and Free(nullptr) do not notify. A callback may replace the process-wide callback, and the next Free invokes that replacement. The existing notify implementation copies the function pointer and releases its global read lock before user code; this ordering is retained and regression checked.

Safe invalid StorageAddress inputs are rejected before any callback. This is an explicit Rust safety-domain regression, not a native-invalid-pointer equivalence claim. Tests serialize callback installation and record per-thread events without fabricating reentrant allocator references.
remaining_gaps_and_adaptations: Callbacks receive an opaque StorageAddress in Rust. Arbitrary native void-pointer inspection/mutation during callbacks, same-owner reentrant operations and C++ subclass mutation are not reproduced. This scope compares capture, unwind, event order and callback replacement over the safe owner domain.

Rust callback panic is used as the defined counterpart of a C++ callback exception. Native destructor behavior, cross-thread raw callback-pointer races and exceptions escaping destructors are outside this scope.

MMgrOpt still uses a sparse free-list table, owned AddressSpace backing and temporary Vec bytes for moved Reallocate. Native table allocation/descriptor effects, exact scratch-allocation behavior and all resource-lifetime differences remain open. The canonical table proposal remains read-only next work.

All 73 Standard service tests, including the unchanged huge pool stress, pass normally. Focused strict Miri runs the eight new callback tests, eleven Standard storage tests and nine service-memory cases; no huge unchanged pool stress is claimed under Miri.

The existing 1<<62 AllocateOptimal resource-boundary test and unrelated locale FFI remain outside this focused Miri selection, as documented by the prior shared-storage receipt; complete normal tests include both.
